free_tier.stated: Start your 30-day Snowflake trial with USD 400 in free credits. The documentation states: 'To sign up for a trial account, all you need is a valid email address; no payment information or other qualifying information is required.' AI features are disabled on a self-service trial account until a credit card is added.

egress.terms: Per-byte egress fee for transfers into a different region or cloud platform, with transfers inside the same region free and no ingress fee; the per-byte rate depends on the hosting region and is on the separate pricing guide, not read.

interface_detail: Snowflake CLI, an open-source command line client for SQL execution and for Snowpark, Streamlit and Native App objects, over a configured connection; SnowSQL is the legacy command line client; documented at docs.snowflake.com
tooling: Snowflake CLI (open source, the preferred client) and SnowSQL (legacy client)
chaining: USD 400 of Snowflake credit is a genuine warehouse for a month and is the standard route to loading a large public dataset once; nothing about it composes, because both the credit and the access end on the same day.
limits_note: at USD 2 a credit on AWS US East Standard and 1 credit an hour for an X-Small Gen1 warehouse, the USD 400 buys 200 warehouse-hours, which is 8.3 days of continuous running
binding_note: the 30-day clock ends the USD 400 before any usage ceiling is reached

identity_cost.detail: a valid email address only, with no payment information required at signup; AI features, external network access, hybrid tables and Openflow stay capped until a credit card is added
